item.content:encoded:
Young people with bold ideas for tackling climate change and creating a more sustainable community can apply for the Youth Climate Action Grants 2026, a funding opportunity offered by the City of Melbourne with support from Bloomberg Philanthropies’ Youth Climate Action Fund.

The program provides grants of up to $7,500 for climate and sustainability projects led by young people aged 15 to 25, with projects supported by organisations that work with young people.

The funding is designed to help young people turn their climate ideas into practical initiatives that can create meaningful change within the City of Melbourne municipality.

Applications for the 2026 round will open on Monday, 17 August 2026, and close on Monday, 28 September 2026.

Opportunity Overview

The Youth Climate Action Grants are intended to support young people who are passionate about climate change and want to take practical action in their communities.

The program recognises that young people have an important role to play in developing innovative responses to environmental and sustainability challenges. Rather than simply encouraging young people to discuss climate change, the grants provide financial support to help transform ideas into real projects.

Successful projects may focus on areas such as climate education, community awareness, sustainability initiatives, environmental action and other creative approaches to addressing climate-related challenges.

Key details

  • Opportunity: Youth Climate Action Grants 2026
  • Category: Grant
  • Grant amount: Up to $7,500
  • Target age: Young people aged 15 to 25
  • Project focus: Climate action and sustainability
  • Project leadership: Projects must be led by young people
  • Supporting organisations: Projects must be supported by organisations that work with young people
  • Project location: City of Melbourne municipality
  • Project completion deadline: Projects must be completed by April 2027
  • Applications open: Monday, 17 August 2026
  • Application deadline: Monday, 28 September 2026
  • Information sessions: August and September 2026
  • Application platform: SmartyGrants

About the Youth Climate Action Grants

The City of Melbourne has established the Youth Climate Action Grants to provide young people with an opportunity to take meaningful action on climate change.

According to the City of Melbourne, many young people care deeply about climate change and want to contribute to bold initiatives that make a difference. The grants are intended to help turn that interest and commitment into practical projects.

The 2026 funding round is supported by the Bloomberg Philanthropies Youth Climate Action Fund, which has enabled the City of Melbourne to secure a third round of funding for its Youth Climate Action Grants.

Through this initiative, young people can develop projects that address environmental challenges while contributing to their local community.

What Can the Grant Support?

The program is broad enough to accommodate different types of climate and sustainability projects.

The City of Melbourne specifically highlights examples including:

1. Climate education initiatives

Young people could develop projects designed to educate their peers, schools, community groups or other audiences about climate change and sustainability.

Potential initiatives could include educational workshops, learning activities, community training or youth-focused environmental education programs.

2. Climate awareness campaigns

Projects could focus on increasing awareness of climate change and encouraging people to adopt more sustainable behaviours.

A strong awareness campaign might use community events, digital communication, educational materials, public engagement or other creative approaches to reach its intended audience.

3. On-the-ground climate action

The grants can also support practical initiatives that move beyond awareness and education into direct action.

Applicants with ideas for tangible climate or sustainability projects may use the opportunity to develop and implement their projects within the City of Melbourne municipality.

4. Innovative sustainability projects

Young people with creative ideas for improving sustainability in their communities can also consider whether their proposal fits within the program’s objectives.

The key consideration is that the proposed initiative should have a clear connection to climate action or sustainability and demonstrate how it can create meaningful change.

Who Can Benefit From This Opportunity?

The Youth Climate Action Grants are specifically designed around youth-led climate action.

The program is therefore particularly relevant to young people aged 15 to 25 who have an idea for a climate or sustainability project and want to develop that idea into a practical community initiative.

However, young applicants are not expected to operate completely independently. The program requires projects to be supported by organisations that work with young people.

This structure can provide young people with organisational support while ensuring that young people remain at the centre of the project.

Geographic Eligibility

An important requirement of this opportunity is the location of the proposed project.

The grant information states that:

Grant projects must be delivered within the City of Melbourne municipality.

This means that the funding is intended for projects that will take place within the City of Melbourne municipality rather than projects being delivered elsewhere in Australia or internationally.

Applicants should therefore carefully consider the location and intended beneficiaries of their proposed project before applying.

Age Requirement

The Youth Climate Action Grants support projects led by young people aged 15 to 25 years old.

This age focus makes the program particularly suitable for youth leaders, students, young community organisers and other young people who are interested in developing practical responses to climate and sustainability challenges.

Applicants should carefully review the official application guidelines before submitting an application to confirm all eligibility conditions and requirements.

Is This Opportunity Open to International Applicants?

The opportunity is administered by the City of Melbourne and requires funded projects to be delivered within the City of Melbourne municipality.

The information provided does not indicate that this is a general international grant that can be applied for from any country or continent.

The program is geographically focused on projects within Melbourne, and prospective applicants should therefore consult the official eligibility requirements and application guidelines to determine whether their specific circumstances qualify.

In particular, the project-location requirement is central to eligibility.

Funding Available

Successful projects can receive up to $7,500.

This provides young people and their supporting organisations with financial resources to develop and implement meaningful climate or sustainability initiatives.

Applicants should ensure that their proposed budget is realistic and clearly connected to the activities required to deliver the project.

A strong proposal should demonstrate why the requested funding is necessary and how the funding will contribute to the project’s intended outcomes.

Project Delivery Period

Grant recipients must complete their projects by April 2027.

This means applicants should consider the project timeline carefully when developing their proposals.

A strong project plan should clearly demonstrate:

  1. What the project aims to achieve.
  2. Who will be involved.
  3. Where the project will take place.
  4. What activities will be undertaken.
  5. What resources will be required.
  6. How the grant funding will be used.
  7. What outcomes the project expects to achieve.
  8. How the project will be completed by April 2027.

How to Apply

The City of Melbourne has outlined a straightforward application process.

Step 1: Check your eligibility

Before starting the application, prospective applicants should establish whether they and their proposed project meet the program’s eligibility requirements.

Pay particular attention to the youth age requirement, project leadership requirements, supporting organisation requirement and project-location requirement.

Step 2: Read the application guidelines

Applicants should carefully read the application guidelines and requirements before preparing their submission.

This is an important stage because understanding the requirements can help applicants avoid submitting incomplete or unsuitable proposals.

Step 3: Attend an information session

Information sessions are available to help prospective applicants understand the Youth Climate Action Grants and develop their project ideas.

Attendance is optional, but the sessions may be particularly useful for young people who want additional guidance before submitting an application.

Step 4: Complete the application

Applicants should prepare their proposal and submit it through the official application form.

Applications must be submitted by Monday, 28 September 2026.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day where possible, particularly if they need assistance from a supporting organisation or need additional time to review their application.

Information Sessions

The City of Melbourne is offering several information sessions in August and September 2026.

These sessions are delivered in partnership with the City of Yarra and are intended to help applicants learn more about the grants and receive support in developing and submitting applications.

Wednesday, 19 August 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 6:30pm

Location: Collingwood Library, 11 Stanton Street, Abbotsford

This is an in-person project ideas workshop.

Thursday, 3 September 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 6:30pm

Location: Online

The online meeting link will be provided after registration.

Thursday, 10 September 2026

Time: 5:30pm to 7:00pm

Location: Melbourne Town Hall, 90–120 Swanston Street, Melbourne

This is an in-person information session.

Prospective applicants can register for the sessions through the links provided on the City of Melbourne’s official Youth Climate Action Grants webpage.

Why Young People Should Consider Applying

The Youth Climate Action Grants offer more than financial support.

For young people interested in climate change, sustainability, community development and leadership, developing and delivering a funded project can provide valuable practical experience.

Potential benefits include:

  • Access to funding of up to $7,500 for an eligible project.
  • An opportunity to turn a climate or sustainability idea into a real initiative.
  • Practical experience in project planning and implementation.
  • Experience working with a supporting organisation.
  • An opportunity to engage with other young people and community members.
  • The chance to contribute to climate action within Melbourne.
  • An opportunity to develop leadership and community engagement skills.
  • Practical experience that may strengthen a young person’s future academic or professional profile.
  • The opportunity to create measurable environmental or community impact.

What Could Make a Strong Project Proposal?

Although applicants should follow the official guidelines, a compelling proposal should clearly communicate the problem the project intends to address and explain how the proposed activities will create positive change.

Applicants should consider presenting:

A clear problem

Explain the climate or sustainability issue the project will address.

A practical solution

Describe what the project will actually do rather than relying only on broad statements about climate change.

Clear beneficiaries

Identify who will benefit from the project and why the project is relevant to them.

A realistic implementation plan

Explain how the project will move from an idea to implementation.

A sensible budget

Clearly connect the proposed expenditure to project activities and outcomes.

Measurable outcomes

Explain what the project expects to achieve and, where possible, how those results will be measured.

Youth leadership

Because the grants are specifically designed to support projects led by young people, applicants should clearly demonstrate the role young people will play in designing and delivering the initiative.

Important Deadline

The application period begins on:

Monday, 17 August 2026

The application deadline is:

Monday, 28 September 2026

Applicants should ensure that their completed application is submitted before the deadline.

Grant projects must subsequently be delivered within the City of Melbourne municipality and completed by April 2027.

Application Link

The City of Melbourne provides a preview of the grant application through its SmartyGrants application platform.

Grant application:
Preview the Youth Climate Action Grants application

Applicants should also review the official City of Melbourne Youth Climate Action Grants webpage for the latest guidelines, requirements, updates and information-session details.

City of Melbourne – Youth Climate Action Grants

For more grants, visit the OFY website HERE

Questions and Further Information

Applicants who have questions about the grants can contact the City of Melbourne through the email addresses provided on the official opportunity page:

  • youth@melbourne.vic.gov.au
  • krystel.bendle@melbourne.vic.gov.au

Applicants should use the official contact channels if they require clarification about eligibility, application requirements, project suitability or other aspects of the grant.

Youth Connect Newsletter

Young people interested in this opportunity and other youth services information can also subscribe to the City of Melbourne’s Youth Connect Newsletter.

The newsletter provides updates about youth services and related opportunities.

Important Things to Remember Before Applying

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the following:

  1. Age: The program supports projects led by young people aged 15 to 25.
  2. Project leadership: The project must be led by young people.
  3. Organisational support: Projects must be supported by organisations that work with young people.
  4. Location: Projects must be delivered within the City of Melbourne municipality.
  5. Funding: Grants of up to $7,500 are available.
  6. Project completion: Funded projects must be completed by April 2027.
  7. Application opening: Applications open on 17 August 2026.
  8. Application deadline: Applications close on 28 September 2026.
  9. Guidelines: Applicants should read the full application guidelines before applying.
  10. Information sessions: Optional sessions are available in August and September to help applicants develop their ideas and applications.

Conclusion

The Youth Climate Action Grants 2026 provide young people with an opportunity to move from climate concerns and ideas to practical action.

With grants of up to $7,500, the program can help eligible youth-led projects deliver education initiatives, awareness campaigns, sustainability activities and other forms of practical climate action within the City of Melbourne municipality.

The opportunity is particularly valuable for young people who already have a strong idea but need financial and organisational support to turn that idea into a tangible community project.

Applications open on 17 August 2026 and close on 28 September 2026. Young people considering applying should begin developing their project ideas early, identify an appropriate supporting organisation, review the application requirements and consider attending one of the available information sessions.

For complete eligibility requirements, application guidelines and the latest updates, applicants should consult the official City of Melbourne information before submitting their applications.

item.content:encoded:
The Ralph M. Barford Foundation (RMBF) has launched its 2026 Open Call for Grant Applications, providing an opportunity for eligible organizations and qualified donees in Canada to seek funding for initiatives that align with the Foundation’s priority areas. The 2026 open call is particularly relevant to Canadian organizations working in multiple sclerosis (MS), children’s literacy, and post-secondary scholarships and bursaries. Applicants may request either unrestricted funding to support existing activities or project funding for specialized, new, or expanded initiatives. The Foundation is also open to considering multi-year funding requests. Organizations interested in applying should carefully review the eligibility requirements and prepare for the two-stage application process, which begins with a Letter of Intent (LOI). Only organizations that successfully pass the LOI stage will be invited to submit a full proposal.

About the Ralph M. Barford Foundation 2026 Grant Opportunity

The Ralph M. Barford Foundation is guided by the belief that every individual should have the opportunity to achieve their full potential. Through its 2026 open call, the Foundation is seeking eligible Canadian qualified donees whose work contributes meaningfully to its identified funding priorities. The grant opportunity is designed to support organizations whose activities can demonstrate clear relevance to the Foundation’s focus areas and measurable benefits for the communities and individuals they serve. The 2026 call represents the Foundation’s first open call for grant applications, giving eligible organizations an opportunity to introduce their work and funding needs through a structured application process.

What Areas Does the Ralph M. Barford Foundation Fund?

Applicants must demonstrate that their work aligns with at least one of the Foundation’s three funding focus areas.

1. Multiple Sclerosis

One of the Foundation’s priority areas is multiple sclerosis (MS). Funding consideration in this area includes both research-related activities and programs that have a direct impact on people living with MS.

Eligible work may include:

  • Research and academic initiatives related to multiple sclerosis.
  • Innovative or alternative approaches to MS research.
  • Programs that directly improve the quality of life of people living with MS.
  • Initiatives that improve access to care and support services.
  • Programs designed to enhance the day-to-day wellbeing of people affected by MS.

The inclusion of alternative research approaches means organizations should not necessarily limit their applications to conventional research models if their proposed work offers a meaningful contribution to understanding, addressing, or improving outcomes associated with MS.

2. Children’s Literacy

Children’s literacy is another major funding priority.

The Foundation is interested in programs that help children develop the literacy skills they need to read at grade level by the time they leave elementary school.

Organizations working in this area may therefore focus on initiatives that:

  • Improve children’s reading abilities.
  • Strengthen literacy development during elementary school.
  • Provide additional educational support to children who face literacy challenges.
  • Help children reach age-appropriate or grade-level reading outcomes.
  • Create measurable improvements in children’s access to literacy resources and learning opportunities.

Applicants should clearly explain how their proposed activities contribute to improved literacy outcomes and who is expected to benefit.

3. Post-Secondary Scholarships and Bursaries

The Foundation also supports post-secondary scholarships and/or bursaries.

These two forms of educational assistance have different primary purposes:

  • Scholarships are primarily achievement-based and recognize promising students based on academic or other forms of achievement.
  • Bursaries are primarily needs-based and help students who require financial assistance to access post-secondary education.

Both types of support can help promising students overcome financial or other barriers to pursuing post-secondary education. Organizations seeking funding for scholarship or bursary programs should be prepared to explain how their programs support students and contribute to greater access to post-secondary education.

What Types of Funding Are Available?

The Ralph M. Barford Foundation allows applicants to request funding under two broad categories.

Unrestricted Funding

Unrestricted funding can be used to help sustain an organization’s existing activities and measurable outcomes.

This type of support may be particularly relevant to organizations that already have established programs or activities aligned with RMBF’s priorities and require flexible funding to maintain their work and continue achieving measurable results.

Project Funding

Project funding is intended for a specialized or new initiative.

Organizations applying under this option should clearly describe the proposed project, its objectives, intended beneficiaries, expected outcomes, implementation timeline, and how its impact will be assessed.

Multi-Year Funding

The Foundation is also open to multi-year funding requests. Organizations whose initiatives require more than one year to implement may therefore consider presenting a longer-term funding request where appropriate. Applicants should demonstrate why multi-year support is necessary and explain the anticipated milestones and outcomes over the proposed funding period.

Eligibility Requirements for the 2026 RMBF Grant

Before starting the Letter of Intent form, organizations should ensure that they meet all of the Foundation’s eligibility requirements.

To qualify, an applicant must meet the following conditions:

1. The Organization Must Be a Canadian Qualified Donee

The applicant must be a registered charity or another type of qualified donee in Canada.

This means the opportunity is not an unrestricted international grant program open to organizations worldwide. The applicant organization must have the appropriate status under Canada’s qualified donee framework.

Organizations should verify their eligibility status before investing significant time in preparing an application.

2. The Organization’s Work Must Match a Funding Focus Area

The organization must be working in at least one of the Foundation’s identified areas:

  • Multiple sclerosis.
  • Children’s literacy.
  • Post-secondary scholarships and/or bursaries.

An organization may therefore be eligible based on its work in one of these areas, but it should be able to demonstrate a clear connection between its activities and the Foundation’s funding priorities.

3. The Funding Request Must Fit an Eligible Funding Type

The requested funding must be either:

  • Unrestricted funding to sustain existing activities and measurable outcomes; or
  • Project funding for a specialized or new initiative.

Multi-year requests may also be considered.

4. The Letter of Intent Must Be Submitted by an Authorized Person

The person submitting the Letter of Intent must either be an authorized signing officer of the organization or have permission from an authorized signing officer to submit the application.

Organizations should therefore make sure that the person responsible for submitting the LOI has the appropriate authority before the application is finalized.

How the 2026 Application Process Works

The Ralph M. Barford Foundation uses a two-stage application process.

Applicants do not immediately submit a full grant proposal. Instead, the process begins with a Letter of Intent.

Stage 1: Letter of Intent

The Letter of Intent is designed to give RMBF enough information to determine whether the organization is eligible and whether its proposed activities fit the Foundation’s funding priorities.

The LOI therefore serves as an initial screening stage.

Organizations should use this stage to communicate the essential information about their organization and proposed funding request, while demonstrating a strong connection between their work and RMBF’s focus areas.

Letter of Intent deadline: Monday, October 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

The online submission form will close at the stated deadline. Organizations are encouraged to submit their applications early rather than waiting until the final hours.

All LOI applicants, regardless of whether they are successful, will be notified of the outcome on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

Stage 2: Full Proposal

The full proposal stage is invitation-only.

Organizations cannot independently proceed to the full proposal stage without first receiving an invitation following a successful Letter of Intent.

On Thursday, October 15, 2026, organizations invited to submit a full proposal will receive a private application link.

Invited organizations will also be asked to schedule a 30-minute introductory call with the Foundation team between October 19 and October 30, 2026.

This call provides applicants with an opportunity to ask questions and seek clarification that may help them strengthen their full application.

The deadline for the full proposal is:

Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

What Information Is Required in the Full Proposal?

Organizations invited to submit a full proposal should expect the application to build on the information provided in the Letter of Intent.

The full proposal will require applicants to provide additional details concerning the proposed activities, anticipated impact, implementation and evaluation.

Key areas include:

Anticipated Outcomes

Applicants will need to describe the expected outcomes of the activities they are seeking funding for.

This should include information about:

  • What the organization expects to accomplish.
  • Who will benefit from the funded activities.
  • What changes or improvements the funding is expected to produce.
  • How the organization will determine whether its objectives have been achieved.

Evaluation of Impact

Applicants will also need to explain how the impact of their activities will be evaluated.

A strong proposal should therefore go beyond simply describing what an organization plans to do. It should demonstrate how the organization intends to determine whether those activities are actually producing meaningful results.

Timeline and Milestones

The full application will also request an anticipated timeline for the proposed activities.

Organizations should identify:

  • Major activities.
  • Implementation periods.
  • Key milestones.
  • Expected completion dates.
  • Important stages in the delivery of the project or program.

A clear timeline can help demonstrate that the organization has considered how the proposed initiative will be implemented.

Financial Documentation

Applicants should also be prepared to submit relevant financial information.

The application may require:

  • Financial statements.
  • A project or organizational budget.
  • Other supporting materials where appropriate.

Applicants should ensure that their financial documents are accurate, current, and consistent with the funding request.

2026 Ralph M. Barford Foundation Grant Timeline

The application process follows a clearly defined schedule.

Week of August 10, 2026

The 2026 open call launches, and the Letter of Intent form becomes available online.

October 5, 2026

Letter of Intent submission deadline.

All LOIs must be submitted online by 11:59 p.m. ET.

October 15, 2026

All LOI applicants will receive notification of their application status.

Organizations selected to proceed to the next stage will receive the full application link and an invitation to schedule a short Zoom call with the RMBF team.

October 19–30, 2026

Short introductory Zoom calls will take place between the Foundation team and organizations invited to submit full proposals.

November 5, 2026

Full application deadline.

Invited organizations must submit their complete proposals by 11:59 p.m. ET.

Mid-December 2026

Final grant decisions will be communicated to applicants.

Mid-to-Late December 2026

Funding is expected to be dispersed to successful organizations.

Important Dates at a Glance

Stage Date
Open call launches Week of August 10, 2026
Letter of Intent deadline October 5, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET
LOI results and full-proposal invitations October 15, 2026
Introductory Zoom calls October 19–30, 2026
Full proposal deadline November 5, 2026, 11:59 p.m. ET
Final funding decisions Mid-December 2026
Funding disbursement Mid-to-late December 2026

How Organizations Can Prepare a Strong Application

Although eligibility is essential, organizations should also focus on demonstrating a strong connection between their work, their proposed funding request, and the Foundation’s priorities.

Clearly Establish Your Alignment

Start by identifying which RMBF focus area your work addresses.

Your application should make it easy for reviewers to understand why your organization and proposed activities fit within the Foundation’s priorities.

Define the Problem You Are Addressing

Clearly explain the challenge or need your organization is responding to.

For example, an organization working in children’s literacy should explain the literacy challenge it is addressing and why its intervention is necessary. Similarly, an organization working with people affected by MS should explain the relevant quality-of-life, care, wellbeing, research, or academic need.

Identify the People Who Will Benefit

Be specific about the intended beneficiaries.

Explain:

  • Who they are.
  • How many people are expected to benefit, where possible.
  • What needs they have.
  • How the proposed activities will improve their circumstances.

Establish Measurable Outcomes

The Foundation specifically asks about anticipated outcomes and how impact will be evaluated.

Applicants should therefore consider measurable indicators that can demonstrate progress.

Instead of simply stating that a program will “improve literacy,” for example, an applicant could explain the specific reading outcomes it intends to achieve and how those outcomes will be measured.

Prepare a Realistic Budget

The budget should correspond closely to the proposed activities.

Applicants should ensure that:

  • Costs are clearly explained.
  • The requested amount is reasonable for the proposed activities.
  • The budget reflects the timeline.
  • Financial information is consistent throughout the application.

Demonstrate Organizational Capacity

Applicants should also demonstrate that their organization has the appropriate experience, personnel, systems, and resources to deliver the proposed work successfully.

Where relevant, explain previous achievements and the organization’s ability to manage and evaluate funded activities.

Why This Grant Opportunity Matters

The 2026 RMBF open call provides an opportunity for eligible Canadian organizations to seek financial support for work addressing important social and educational priorities.

The Foundation’s three focus areas cover several different forms of impact.

Support for multiple sclerosis research and programs can contribute to improved knowledge, care, quality of life, and wellbeing for people living with MS.

Investment in children’s literacy can help young people develop foundational reading skills that are important for their broader educational development.

Support for post-secondary scholarships and bursaries can help promising students access higher education, particularly where financial barriers may otherwise limit their opportunities.

The Foundation’s willingness to consider both unrestricted and project funding also gives eligible organizations some flexibility in presenting their funding needs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can apply for the RMBF 2026 grant?

The open call is intended for registered charities and other qualified donees in Canada whose work aligns with at least one of the Foundation’s funding priorities.

Can organizations outside Canada apply?

The eligibility criteria specify that the applicant must be a registered charity or other qualified donee in Canada. Therefore, organizations should not assume that an organization based outside Canada is eligible simply because its work relates to one of RMBF’s focus areas.

What areas does RMBF fund?

The Foundation’s 2026 focus areas are:

  1. Multiple sclerosis.
  2. Children’s literacy.
  3. Post-secondary scholarships and/or bursaries.

Can an organization request unrestricted funding?

Yes. RMBF accepts requests for unrestricted funding intended to sustain existing activities and measurable outcomes.

Can applicants request project funding?

Yes. Project funding can be requested for a specialized or new initiative.

Does RMBF consider multi-year funding?

Yes. The Foundation is open to considering multi-year requests.

Is the full proposal open to everyone?

No. Full proposals are accepted by invitation only after a successful Letter of Intent.

What is the Letter of Intent deadline?

The Letter of Intent must be submitted by Monday, October 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

When will LOI applicants receive a decision?

All LOI applicants will be notified on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

When is the full proposal deadline?

Invited organizations must submit their full proposals by Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

When will final funding decisions be made?

Final funding decisions are expected in mid-December 2026, with funding expected to be dispersed in mid-to-late December 2026.

For more information click HERE

Application and Further Information

Organizations should review the Foundation’s official information and FAQ before beginning the application process. nFor questions and additional information, applicants can consult the Ralph M. Barford Foundation FAQ and the Foundation’s application materials. The Letter of Intent should be completed carefully and submitted before the October 5 deadline. Because the online form closes at the deadline, applicants are encouraged to avoid leaving submission until the last minute.

Conclusion

The Ralph M. Barford Foundation Open Call 2026 offers eligible Canadian qualified donees an opportunity to seek grant funding for initiatives that align with the Foundation’s priorities in multiple sclerosis, children’s literacy, and post-secondary scholarships and bursaries. The opportunity provides flexibility through two funding pathways: unrestricted funding for sustaining existing activities and measurable outcomes, and project funding for specialized or new initiatives. Multi-year requests may also be considered. However, organizations should pay close attention to the two-stage application process. The first and most immediate step is the Letter of Intent, which must be submitted by October 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Only organizations that receive an invitation following the LOI review will proceed to the full proposal stage. Eligible organizations should begin preparing early by confirming their qualified donee status, identifying how their work aligns with RMBF’s focus areas, defining measurable outcomes, preparing relevant financial information, and ensuring that an authorized person submits the LOI. For organizations working in the Foundation’s priority areas, this open call represents an opportunity to seek financial support for initiatives designed to produce meaningful and measurable benefits for individuals, students, children, and communities in Canada.

Deadline for Letter of Intent: October 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Full proposal deadline for invited organizations: November 5, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a graduate from Central, Eastern, or Southeastern Europe looking for an opportunity to pursue a Master’s degree, PhD, or research stay in Germany? The Free State of Bavaria is offering one-year scholarships for the 2027/28 academic year to eligible graduates from selected European countries.

The scholarship supports postgraduate studies and research at state or state-funded higher education institutions in Bavaria. It is designed to strengthen academic exchange, scientific cooperation, and educational relationships between Bavaria and participating countries.

Successful applicants will receive a monthly scholarship of €992, equivalent to €11,904 per year. Those with at least one child may also qualify for a family allowance of €160 per month, bringing the total support to €1,152 per month or €13,824 per year.

Application deadline for first-time applicants: December 1, 2026.

Who Can Apply?

The scholarship is available to graduates who hold citizenship from the following countries:

  • Bulgaria
  • Croatia
  • Czechia
  • Hungary
  • Poland
  • Romania
  • Russia
  • Serbia
  • Slovakia
  • Ukraine

Applicants must generally have their permanent residence in their home country at the time of application.

For Master’s applicants, the normal age requirement is being under 30 years old at the time the scholarship begins on October 1, 2027. PhD applicants must generally be under 35 years old. Justified exceptions may be considered in certain circumstances.

What Does the Scholarship Support?

The scholarship can support:

  • Complete postgraduate Master’s programs in Bavaria.
  • PhD/doctoral programs at eligible Bavarian institutions.
  • A one-year research stay in Bavaria as part of a PhD being completed in the applicant’s home country.

The selected program must mainly take place in Bavaria and require the applicant to relocate there.

The scholarship does not cover an exchange year in Bavaria that forms part of a Master’s program in the applicant’s home country or fee-based continuing education programs for experienced professionals.

Scholarship Benefits

Selected scholars will receive:

  • €992 per month.
  • €11,904 per year in standard scholarship funding.
  • An additional €160 per month family allowance may be available to scholars with at least one child.
  • Up to €1,152 per month for eligible recipients receiving the family allowance.
  • Up to €13,824 per year including the family allowance.
  • Funding can generally be extended twice for up to three years, subject to eligibility and approval.

For PhD programs in Bavaria, an additional extension of one or two semesters may be possible in exceptional and well-justified circumstances.

Applicants should note that travel expenses are not covered. Scholars are responsible for their travel to Bavaria and must arrange their own visa.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should meet the following requirements:

Academic excellence

Applicants must demonstrate well above-average academic performance at their university in their home country.

Academic achievements such as excellent grades, scholarships, awards, publications, lectures, and research experience can strengthen an application.

Language proficiency

Applicants must have sufficient German and/or English language skills for their proposed study or research project. The program generally expects language proficiency around C1 level under the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

Academic connection

The proposed Master’s or research project should have a meaningful connection to the applicant’s previous degree and future academic or professional goals.

Enrollment

Applicants do not necessarily have to be enrolled at a Bavarian university when submitting the scholarship application. However, successful applicants must enroll at their selected Bavarian institution during the scholarship period.

Selection Criteria

The scholarship is competitive, and meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee selection.

The selection committee considers factors such as:

  • Previous academic performance.
  • Scholarships, prizes, publications, and academic achievements.
  • Motivation for postgraduate study in Bavaria.
  • Relevance of the proposed program to the applicant’s first degree and career goals.
  • Quality and scientific relevance of a proposed PhD project.
  • German and/or English language proficiency.
  • Additional foreign-language skills.
  • Internships and practical experience.
  • International study or work experience.
  • Participation in conferences and seminars.
  • Further professional or academic training.
  • Voluntary work and community involvement.
  • Academic supervision arrangements for PhD applicants.
  • International cooperation between the applicant’s home university and a Bavarian institution.

Applicants should also be prepared to participate in a possible online interview.

Required Application Documents

First-time applicants must submit their applications online through the StipSys system.

Required documents include:

  1. Motivation letter of 1–2 pages in German or English.
  2. Proof of German and/or English language proficiency.
  3. University degree certificate and transcript of records, with certified translation where required.
  4. Proof of citizenship, such as a passport or national identity card.
  5. Tabular CV in German or English.
  6. Documents supporting relevant voluntary work, internships, training, publications, and other achievements.

Supporting documents can include up to 10 relevant documents.

Additional requirements for PhD applicants

Applicants applying for a PhD in Bavaria must also provide:

  • A two-page research project description.
  • A timetable for the overall project.
  • A letter of endorsement from a professor at a Bavarian higher education institution.

Applicants applying for a one-year research stay in Bavaria as part of a PhD in their home country must additionally provide:

  • A letter of recommendation from their PhD supervisor in their home country.

Family allowance

Applicants requesting the family allowance must provide the child’s birth certificate and the required certified translation where applicable.

Application Process

Applications are submitted exclusively online through the StipSys application system.

Applicants are advised to prepare all documents before beginning the online form because the form cannot be temporarily saved and may close automatically after being inactive for too long.

Documents must:

  • Be submitted in PDF format.
  • Be no larger than 5 MB per file.
  • Be combined into one PDF where several documents belong to the same application category.

After submission, applicants will receive confirmation of receipt and an email requesting activation of their StipSys account.

Applicants should carefully review their submission because changes cannot normally be made after the application has been submitted. Any necessary additions must be arranged with the responsible BAYHOST or BTHA contact person.

If multiple applications are submitted, only the most recent application will be considered.

                           Learn more about this opportunity HERE

 Important Deadlines

First-Time Applications

December 1, 2026

This is the main deadline for new applicants applying for the 2027/28 scholarship year.

Late or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Extension Applications

February 28, 2027

This deadline applies to applicants seeking an extension of an existing scholarship.

Selection Timeline

The expected timeline for the 2027/28 scholarship is:

  • December 2026 – March 2027: Review and evaluation of applications.
  • April – May 2027: Selection committee meetings.
  • May 2027: Selection results communicated by email.
  • June 15, 2027: General application deadline for certain Bavarian higher education institutions.
  • July 15, 2027: Application deadline for research universities.
  • October 1, 2027: Scholarship program begins.

Applicants should note that university admission deadlines can vary, particularly for individual Master’s programs. The scholarship application and university admission are separate processes.

Additional Conditions

Scholarship recipients must comply with several conditions during their funding period.

With consultation and approval from BAYHOST/BTHA, scholars may generally have additional income of up to €800 gross per month on average. A combination with another scholarship may also be possible under the stated conditions.

Scholarship payments are normally transferred at the beginning of each month. Recipients need to provide appropriate bank account details, residential information in Bavaria, and their German tax identification number after registering their residence.

Scholars are also required to maintain their enrollment and submit current certificates of enrollment. They may be required to participate in program activities such as seminars, meetings, and the annual reception.

Tips for Applicants

Applicants can improve their chances by preparing well in advance.

Research your university early: Identify suitable Bavarian universities and Master’s or PhD programs before submitting the scholarship application.

Prepare a strong motivation letter: Clearly explain why you want to study in Bavaria, how the program connects to your previous education, and how it supports your future career.

Highlight your achievements: Include academic awards, publications, research, internships, conferences, professional experience, and other relevant accomplishments.

Document your voluntary work: Community involvement, NGO activities, student organizations, and other voluntary activities may contribute positively to your application.

For PhD applicants, contact supervisors early: A Bavarian professor’s endorsement is required, so applicants should not wait until the deadline to establish academic contact.

                                                    APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Study and Research in Bavaria Scholarship 2027/28 offers academically strong graduates from eligible European countries the opportunity to pursue postgraduate education or research in Bavaria with significant financial support.

The program is particularly suitable for graduates planning a Master’s degree, PhD, or qualifying one-year research stay and who can demonstrate excellent academic performance, strong language skills, clear career goals, and meaningful academic or professional experience.

Because the scholarship is competitive and late or incomplete applications are not accepted, prospective applicants should begin preparing their documents and researching suitable Bavarian institutions well ahead of the deadline.

First-time application deadline: December 1, 2026.

Extension application deadline: February 28, 2027.

For Czech applicants, the relevant contact is the Bayerisch-Tschechische Hochschulagentur (BTHA). Applicants from all other eligible countries should contact BAYHOST for scholarship-related guidance.

item.content:encoded:
The Western Balkans Meet Japan: A Bridge into the Future program is part of the MIRAI initiative, which has been running since 2018.

The exchange focuses on creating meaningful connections between young people from the Western Balkans and Japan. Through academic discussions, institutional visits, cultural activities, and interaction with Japanese society, participants will gain a broader understanding of Japan’s approaches to peacebuilding, reconciliation, international cooperation, and social development.

The 2026/2027 edition will take place in Japan from:

20–26 January 2027

A total of 13 undergraduate or graduate students aged 20 or older will be selected from the Western Balkans.

Eligible participants will come from the following six Western Balkan societies:

  • Albania
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina
  • Kosovo
  • Montenegro
  • North Macedonia
  • Serbia

What Is the Aim of the Western Balkans Meet Japan Program?

The program is more than a cultural trip. It is designed to encourage young people to develop knowledge, relationships, and skills that can contribute to peace and cooperation in the Western Balkans.

The main objectives include:

1. Deepening Understanding of Japan

Participants will have the opportunity to learn about Japan, its society, culture, policies, institutions, and approaches to international cooperation.

The experience allows participants to move beyond learning about Japan from books or online resources by providing opportunities to experience Japanese society directly.

2. Promoting Peacebuilding and Reconciliation

A central element of the exchange is learning about Japan’s experience with peacebuilding, reconciliation, and international cooperation.

Participants will explore how societies can address difficult historical experiences and work toward peaceful coexistence.

3. Strengthening Mutual Understanding

The program creates opportunities for young people from the Western Balkans and Japan to interact, exchange perspectives, and learn from one another.

This intercultural experience is intended to reduce misunderstandings and strengthen relationships between people from different backgrounds.

4. Encouraging Regional Cooperation

Participants from six Western Balkan societies will have the opportunity to interact with one another while in Japan.

The experience can help strengthen relationships among young people from the region and encourage future cooperation across national borders.

5. Building Future International Partnerships

The program aims to create a foundation for long-term friendship and cooperation between Japan and the Western Balkans.

Participants can develop networks with other young leaders, academics, institutions, and people involved in international cooperation.

The program is specifically targeted at young people from the Western Balkans.

Applicants must satisfy the eligibility requirements established for the exchange.

1. Current University Students

Applicants must currently be enrolled in:

  • An undergraduate program
  • A graduate program
  • A PhD program

Applicants must be 20 years old or older at the time of application.

2. Applicants Must Be From the Western Balkans

Applicants must live in one of the participating Western Balkan societies and hold a passport issued by one of the WB6 countries:

Applicants who hold Japanese nationality are not eligible.

3. Good Command of English

Applicants must have a good command of English, as the program involves academic discussions, communication, presentations, cultural exchange, and interaction with participants and institutions.

4. Interest in Japan

Applicants should demonstrate genuine interest in Japan and be motivated to learn about Japanese society, culture, policies, and international cooperation.

Applicants who already have demonstrated connections with Japan may have an advantage.

Such connections could include:

  • Previous studies related to Japan
  • Participation in Japanese cultural activities
  • Academic or professional experiences related to Japan
  • Other relevant Japan-related experiences

5. Academic Achievement

Applicants should demonstrate good academic performance.

Academic achievements will form part of the overall assessment of candidates.

6. Social Activism and Community Engagement

The program is also interested in young people who are actively engaged in their communities.

Applicants should demonstrate involvement in activities that show initiative, leadership, civic engagement, volunteering, advocacy, or other forms of social participation.

7. Interest in Peace and Reconciliation

Applicants should respect the principles of reconciliation and cooperation in the Western Balkans.

Candidates with experience or demonstrated interest in areas such as:

  • Dealing with the past
  • Peacebuilding
  • Reconciliation
  • Regional cooperation
  • Intercultural learning

are particularly encouraged to apply.

8. Valid Passport

Applicants must have a valid passport.

This is particularly important because the selected participants will travel internationally to Japan.

What Will Participants Experience in Japan?

The seven-day exchange is expected to combine academic learning, cultural activities, institutional visits, and opportunities for personal interaction.

Participants can expect to learn about Japan through direct engagement rather than simply classroom-based instruction.

Activities may include opportunities to:

  • Visit Japanese institutions
  • Participate in academic discussions
  • Learn about peacebuilding and reconciliation
  • Explore Japanese culture and society
  • Engage with Japanese students and young people
  • Learn about international cooperation
  • Participate in cultural exchange activities
  • Visit locations connected to Japan’s history and peacebuilding experience
  • Develop relationships with other participants
  • Exchange ideas about the future of the Western Balkans

The previous edition provides an indication of the type of experience participants may receive.

Highlights From the Previous Western Balkans Meet Japan Exchange

During the 2025/2026 exchange, 13 young people from the Western Balkans travelled to Japan from 13–19 February 2026.

They were selected through a competitive process involving more than 1,000 applicants.

The previous participants visited important institutions and locations, including:

  • JICA Headquarters
  • Sophia University
  • Peace Memorial Park in Hiroshima

Through these activities, participants explored Japan’s approaches to:

  • Peacebuilding
  • Reconciliation
  • International cooperation
  • Intercultural dialogue
  • Conflict resolution

The previous exchange combined academic discussions with cultural activities and personal reflection.

The experience also helped participants create international connections and encouraged them to become promoters of peace and cooperation within their communities.

Costs Covered by the Program

One of the major advantages of the Western Balkans Meet Japan exchange is that many of the major costs associated with participating in the program are covered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan.

Covered expenses include:

International Airfare

The program covers round-trip international economy-class airfare to Japan.

Travel Insurance

Participants will receive overseas travel and accident insurance during the program.

Accommodation

Accommodation in Japan during the official program will be covered.

Transportation in Japan

Transportation required for scheduled program activities in Japan will be covered.

Meals

Meals during the official program are covered.

Admission Fees

Admission fees associated with scheduled activities and visits in Japan will also be covered.

Expenses Participants Must Pay

Although major program-related expenses are covered, participants should understand that not every personal expense is paid for by the organizers.

Participants are responsible for their own:

  • Passport costs
  • Visa application and acquisition costs, where applicable
  • Vaccination expenses
  • Excess baggage charges
  • Travel expenses between their home and the designated airport
  • Souvenirs
  • Personal purchases
  • Other personal expenses before or during the program

Applicants should therefore prepare financially for expenses that fall outside the official program coverage.

Visa Information

Participants from some of the participating Western Balkan societies will need a visa to travel to Japan.

According to the program information, participants from:

  • Albania
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina
  • Kosovo
  • Montenegro

will need to apply for a visa.

The organizers will provide selected participants with further information about the visa application process once the relevant arrangements have been determined.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they have sufficient time to obtain the necessary travel documents if selected.

Why This Youth Exchange Is Important

The Western Balkans has a history of complex political, social, and cultural relationships. Programs that bring young people together can play an important role in encouraging dialogue and building relationships across borders.

The Western Balkans Meet Japan program provides young people with an opportunity to examine these issues from an international perspective.

Through exposure to Japan’s experience with peacebuilding and reconciliation, participants can gain new perspectives that may be relevant to their own communities.

The program also places considerable emphasis on people-to-people connections.

Rather than focusing only on formal academic learning, the exchange encourages participants to communicate, share experiences, understand different perspectives, and develop lasting relationships.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Program Western Balkans Meet Japan: A Bridge into the Future
Program Type Youth Exchange Program
Organizers Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan (MOFA) and RYCO
Framework MIRAI Program
Program Dates 20–26 January 2027
Duration 7 days
Number of Participants 13
Minimum Age 20 years
Study Level Undergraduate, Graduate or PhD
Eligible Countries Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia
Language English
Location Japan
Nationality Restriction Applicants must hold a passport from one of the WB6 societies; Japanese nationals are not eligible
International Flight Covered
Accommodation Covered
Meals During Program Covered
Transportation in Japan Covered
Travel/Accident Insurance Covered
Activity Admission Fees Covered
Visa Required for participants from certain countries
Application Deadline 31st August,2026

Important Things Applicants Should Know

Before applying, prospective participants should carefully consider the following requirements:

  1. You must be at least 20 years old at the time of application.
  2. You must currently be enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate, or PhD program.
  3. You must live in one of the six participating Western Balkan societies.
  4. You must hold a passport issued by one of the WB6 countries.
  5. You must have a good command of English.
  6. You should have good academic achievements.
  7. You should demonstrate social activism or community engagement.
  8. You should have a genuine interest in Japan.
  9. You must respect the principles of reconciliation and cooperation in the Western Balkans.
  10. You must have a valid passport.
  11. Applicants with experience related to Japan, peacebuilding, dealing with the past, reconciliation, regional cooperation, or intercultural learning are particularly encouraged to apply.
  12. Applicants should be prepared to cover personal expenses that are not included in the program’s financial support.

                                       LEARN MORE HERE

Application Deadline

 31st August,2026.

Because the program takes place in January 2027, prospective applicants should avoid waiting until the last minute to prepare their documents.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This program could be particularly suitable for young people who are:

  • University students from the Western Balkans
  • Interested in Japan and Japanese culture
  • Interested in peacebuilding and reconciliation
  • Active in their communities
  • Interested in regional cooperation
  • Interested in international relations
  • Passionate about intercultural dialogue
  • Interested in conflict resolution
  • Engaged in youth leadership
  • Interested in dealing with the past
  • Interested in learning from international experiences
  • Interested in building international networks

Candidates who can demonstrate how they intend to use their experience to contribute to their communities may be especially well positioned for this type of exchange.

                                                      APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Western Balkans Meet Japan: A Bridge into the Future 2026/2027 program offers 13 young people from the Western Balkans the opportunity to travel to Japan for a seven-day educational, cultural, and academic exchange.

Beyond the opportunity to experience Japan, participants will explore important issues surrounding peacebuilding, reconciliation, intercultural dialogue, regional cooperation, and international understanding.

With major program expenses such as international airfare, accommodation, meals, transportation, insurance, and scheduled activity fees covered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, the exchange provides a valuable opportunity for eligible young people to gain international exposure while developing relationships that can contribute to future cooperation between Japan and the Western Balkans.

For students aged 20 and above from Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, this program represents an opportunity to learn, connect, exchange ideas, and become part of a wider network of young people working toward a more peaceful and cooperative future.
