item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships 2026, an annual scholarship programme designed to recognize and support outstanding women pursuing education in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Through the Endeavour Women in Tech initiative, Endeavour Infrastructure aims to help address the continued underrepresentation of women across STEM fields while supporting students who have already demonstrated exceptional academic performance, research ability, technical achievement, or advocacy related to science and technology.

For the 2026 cycle, selected recipients may receive scholarship awards of up to $10,000 to support their education.

The opportunity is open to both:

  • Women graduating from high school and entering their first year of college in fall 2026
  • Current undergraduate and graduate students attending a U.S. college or university

Applicants must have a minimum 3.5 GPA and demonstrate exceptional work, research, and/or advocacy in STEM.

The application deadline is September 8, 2026.

About the Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships

The Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships, often associated with the Endeavour Women in Tech initiative, were created to recognize talented women pursuing STEM education and encourage their continued advancement in technology, engineering, science, mathematics, and related fields.

Endeavour Infrastructure describes the scholarship programme as part of its wider commitment to supporting, advancing, and empowering women in technology and infrastructure.

The programme is built around a simple reality: although women continue to make major contributions to innovation and scientific progress, they remain underrepresented in many STEM disciplines.

The scholarship therefore seeks to identify students who are not only succeeding academically but also demonstrating meaningful engagement in their chosen STEM areas.

This could include significant:

  • Academic work
  • Research
  • Technical projects
  • STEM advocacy
  • Leadership
  • Innovation
  • Community engagement related to STEM

Scholarship Value

Each year, Endeavour awards scholarships of:

Up to $10,000 per recipient

Applicants should note that the exact amount may vary between recipients.

Past scholarship awards have included amounts ranging from $2,000 to $10,000, demonstrating that the programme may offer different funding levels based on the selection process and available resources.

For example, previous recipients have received awards of:

  • $10,000
  • $5,000
  • $3,000
  • $2,000

The 2026 programme states that outstanding women pursuing STEM degrees can receive up to $10,000.

Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarship Impact

Since the programme’s development, Endeavour Women in Tech has provided significant support to students pursuing science and technology education.

The programme reports that it has:

  • Awarded more than $85,000
  • Supported 15 scholarship recipients
  • Reached students across 12 universities
  • Been operating since 2022

These figures demonstrate the growing reach of the programme and its continued commitment to supporting women entering or progressing through STEM education.

Who Can Apply?

The 2026 Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships are designed for women studying or preparing to study STEM subjects at universities and colleges in the United States.

There are two main applicant categories.

1. Incoming University Students

Women graduating from high school and preparing to enter their freshman year of college in fall 2026 may apply.

Candidates must be entering a U.S. college or university.

This pathway is particularly relevant to high school students who have already built an impressive academic or extracurricular record in science, technology, engineering, or mathematics.

2. Current University and Graduate Students

Women who are already studying at a U.S. college or university may also apply.

Eligible students can include current:

  • Undergraduate students
  • Graduate students

Applicants should be pursuing STEM-related studies and meet the required academic standard.

Minimum GPA Requirement

Applicants must have a minimum:

3.5 GPA

This is an important eligibility requirement.

Candidates should therefore ensure that their current academic record meets or exceeds this threshold before submitting an application.

The scholarship is competitive, so applicants with strong grades should also focus on demonstrating how their STEM experience extends beyond academic performance alone.

Eligible STEM Fields

The scholarship is intended for women pursuing education in:

  • Science
  • Technology
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics

The supplied programme information does not provide a complete list of eligible majors.

However, STEM programmes may potentially include areas such as:

Science

Students may be studying disciplines connected to the natural or applied sciences.

Technology

Technology-related majors may include areas connected to computing, information systems, software, emerging technologies, or other technical fields.

Engineering

Engineering applicants may come from a range of engineering disciplines.

Mathematics

Students pursuing mathematics or strongly quantitative programmes may also be relevant.

Applicants should consult the official application page if they are uncertain whether their specific academic major falls within the programme’s definition of STEM.

What the Scholarship Looks for

The scholarship does not appear to be based solely on grades.

Applicants are expected to demonstrate:

Exceptional work, research, and/or advocacy in STEM.

This creates several possible ways to build a strong application.

Exceptional STEM Work

Applicants may be able to demonstrate their abilities through substantial academic, technical, or practical work.

Examples might include:

  • STEM projects
  • Technical competitions
  • Engineering design work
  • Programming projects
  • Scientific initiatives
  • Academic projects
  • Innovation-related activities

Applicants should focus on explaining what they personally contributed and what they learned or achieved.

Research Experience

Research is specifically highlighted by Endeavour as one of the areas that may strengthen an application.

Research experience could potentially include:

  • Laboratory research
  • University research projects
  • Independent research
  • Faculty-assisted projects
  • Research internships
  • Conference presentations
  • Scientific publications
  • Technical investigations

A candidate should clearly communicate the purpose of the research, their role, and any outcomes generated.

STEM Advocacy

The scholarship also welcomes applicants who have demonstrated advocacy in STEM.

Advocacy could involve work intended to:

  • Encourage girls to pursue STEM
  • Improve access to science and technology education
  • Support women in technical careers
  • Promote STEM learning in underserved communities
  • Mentor younger students
  • Organize science or technology programmes
  • Support diversity and inclusion within STEM

This element makes the scholarship particularly interesting because applicants do not necessarily need to rely entirely on research achievements.

Leadership and community impact may also strengthen the application.

Why Women in STEM Matter

The Endeavour Women in Tech initiative is grounded in the recognition that women remain underrepresented in many areas of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

Supporting women in STEM can have effects far beyond individual scholarships.

Increasing the participation of women can contribute to:

  • More diverse research teams
  • Broader perspectives in technology development
  • Greater representation in engineering
  • More inclusive innovation
  • Stronger pathways for future women scientists and technologists
  • More diverse leadership across technology and infrastructure

Financial support can also reduce barriers that make it difficult for talented students to continue developing their education.

The scholarship therefore combines financial assistance with recognition of women already demonstrating excellence and promise in STEM.

Past Scholarship Recipients

Previous Endeavour Women in Tech scholarship recipients have attended several prominent universities.

Past awardees have studied at institutions including:

  • Colorado School of Mines
  • Massachusetts Institute of Technology
  • University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
  • San Jose State University
  • University of Maryland
  • University of Colorado Boulder
  • Stanford University
  • Villanova University
  • Columbia University
  • Cornell University
  • University of Alabama
  • Howard University

Award amounts have varied depending on the year and recipient.

Some previous students received the maximum $10,000, while others received smaller awards.

This reinforces the importance of describing the programme accurately as offering up to $10,000, rather than assuming every selected student receives the maximum amount.

Application Categories

Endeavour provides separate application pathways for:

Incoming University Students

This application is intended for students graduating from high school and beginning their first year of university.

APPLY HERE

Current University Students

This route is designed for students who are currently enrolled in college or graduate study.

APPLY HERE

Applicants should use the application link corresponding to their current educational status.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because the scholarship recognizes exceptional STEM achievement, candidates should prepare an application that goes beyond simply listing grades and activities.

1. Highlight Your Strongest STEM Achievement

Choose one or two accomplishments that genuinely demonstrate your potential.

This could be:

  • Research
  • A technical project
  • A scientific discovery
  • An engineering design
  • A coding project
  • Advocacy
  • Community leadership
  • A STEM-focused initiative

Explain your actual contribution.

2. Demonstrate Impact

Selection committees are more likely to understand an achievement when applicants show what changed because of their work.

Where possible, explain:

  • What problem you addressed
  • What you personally did
  • What skills you used
  • Who benefited
  • What outcome resulted

Concrete examples are generally more persuasive than broad claims such as “I am passionate about STEM.”

3. Explain Your STEM Direction

Applicants should be prepared to show how their current studies connect with their future ambitions.

Consider explaining:

  • Why you chose your STEM field
  • What issues you want to solve
  • What kind of work you hope to pursue
  • How the scholarship could help you continue your development

4. Highlight Advocacy Where Relevant

Students who have supported other women, girls, or underrepresented communities in STEM should describe that work clearly.

Include specific examples of mentoring, outreach, education, advocacy, or leadership.

5. Check Your GPA

Make sure your academic record demonstrates the required minimum:

3.5 GPA

Applicants below the stated threshold would not meet the published eligibility criteria.

Application Deadline

Applications for the 2026 Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships close on:

September 8, 2026

Applicants should submit before the deadline wherever possible.

Waiting until the final hours can create unnecessary risk if technical difficulties, missing materials, or application errors arise.

Important Information at a Glance

Programme: Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships 2026

Scholarship value: Up to $10,000

Academic focus: STEM

Minimum GPA: 3.5

Applicant levels: Incoming college freshmen, current undergraduate students, and graduate students

Study location: U.S. college or university

Selection emphasis: Exceptional STEM work, research, and/or advocacy

Application deadline: September 8, 2026

Why You Should Apply

The Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarship provides more than financial assistance.

Receiving the award also offers recognition of the applicant’s work and potential in a field where women remain underrepresented.

For an incoming college student, the scholarship can provide meaningful financial support at the beginning of a STEM degree.

For an undergraduate or graduate student, it can provide recognition for research, technical achievement, or advocacy already underway.

Applicants who have strong academic performance and a clear record of STEM engagement should therefore seriously consider submitting an application.

Conclusion

The Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarships 2026 offer an important opportunity for women pursuing science, technology, engineering, and mathematics at colleges and universities in the United States.

Selected recipients may receive up to $10,000, helping support their continued academic and professional development.

The scholarship is open to women graduating from high school and entering college in fall 2026, as well as current undergraduate and graduate students studying at U.S. institutions.

Applicants must maintain at least a 3.5 GPA and demonstrate exceptional STEM work, research, and/or advocacy.

Since 2022, Endeavour Women in Tech has awarded more than $85,000 to 15 recipients attending 12 universities, demonstrating an ongoing commitment to helping women advance in STEM.

Applications for the 2026 cycle close on September 8, 2026.

For women already building strong academic, research, technical, or advocacy records in STEM, the Endeavour Women in Tech Scholarship provides an opportunity to receive financial support while gaining recognition for their achievements and future potential.

To learn more about this opportunity, CLICK HERE. 

For more global scholarship opportunities, VISIT HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey is a fully funded leadership development opportunity for mid-career women working across health and interconnected sectors in Southern Africa. The 12-month programme is designed to help women leaders strengthen their voice, influence, leadership capacity and ability to create meaningful and sustainable health impact.

Through a combination of virtual learning, mentoring, one-on-one executive coaching, experiential learning and a self-directed Health Leadership Project, participants will gain practical tools for addressing complex health challenges while building a powerful regional network of women leaders.

The programme is offered at no cost to selected participants, with WomenLift Health covering programme costs, including travel and lodging for the required in-person experiences.

Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM CAT.

Key Details of the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey

  • Programme: WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey
  • Duration: Approximately 12 months
  • Format: Hybrid, combining virtual and in-person learning
  • Programme cost: Free
  • Programme learning commitment: Approximately 4–8 hours per month
  • Total learning hours: Approximately 87 hours
  • Cohort size: 35 women leaders in health
  • Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM CAT
  • Region: Southern Africa
  • Eligible countries: Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, eSwatini, Zambia and Zimbabwe
  • Target participants: Mid-career women leaders with 10–25 years of professional experience in Health++
  • Language: English
  • Time-zone requirement: CAT, plus or minus one hour, for at least 75% of the programme
  • Funding: Fully funded, including programme costs, travel and lodging for required in-person experiences

What Is the WomenLift Health Leadership Journey?

The WomenLift Health Leadership Journey is a transformational leadership and learning experience created for professional women working across the health sector and related fields.

The programme provides participants with a structured environment in which they can reflect on their leadership journeys, strengthen their ability to influence others, develop new leadership strategies and work on complex health challenges.

The Southern Africa Leadership Journey is specifically designed for women leaders working in countries across Southern Africa.

Rather than focusing exclusively on technical health knowledge, the programme takes a broader approach to leadership. It recognises that improving health outcomes requires leaders who can work across sectors, understand complex systems, build coalitions and influence institutions.

Participants therefore explore both personal leadership development and systems-level health challenges.

What Makes the 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey Different?

The programme combines several complementary elements rather than relying on traditional classroom-based training.

Participants will have access to:

  1. Intensive leadership learning
  2. Virtual learning touchpoints
  3. Group mentoring
  4. Individual executive coaching
  5. Leadership assessments
  6. In-person experiential learning
  7. A Health Leadership Project
  8. A diverse regional network of women leaders
  9. Opportunities to collaborate across sectors
  10. Continued engagement through a lifelong community

This combination is intended to help participants translate leadership concepts into practical action.

The programme also provides a safe environment for participants to reflect on their experiences, vulnerabilities, strengths and aspirations while learning alongside peers facing similar leadership challenges.

Programme Duration and Format

The 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey is structured as a 12-month programme with both virtual and in-person components.

Participants should expect to dedicate approximately 4–8 hours each month to the Journey.

Across the programme, the estimated total learning commitment is approximately 87 hours, including learning touchpoints and work associated with the Health Leadership Project.

The hybrid structure allows participants to remain engaged with their professional responsibilities while participating in carefully designed leadership-development experiences.

However, participants should understand that the required sessions are considered important components of the programme and that attendance is expected.

Cost: A Fully Funded Leadership Opportunity

One of the most significant advantages of the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey is that it is offered free of charge to selected participants.

WomenLift Health states that programme costs are covered, including:

  • Programme participation
  • Travel associated with required in-person experiences
  • Lodging associated with those experiences

This funding structure is intended to make the leadership-development experience accessible to qualified women leaders without requiring participants to personally finance the programme’s major participation costs.

Because the programme involves live, interactive learning and in-person residencies, selected participants are expected to make the necessary time available for participation.

Who Is the Programme Designed For?

The Southern Africa Leadership Journey is designed for mid-career women leaders working in health and related sectors.

WomenLift Health takes a broad view of what constitutes health leadership.

Rather than limiting participation to physicians, nurses or public health professionals, the programme recognises that sustainable health improvements depend on action across multiple interconnected areas.

Participants may therefore come from different professional sectors and disciplines that influence health outcomes.

These can include:

  • Public health
  • Healthcare
  • Medicine
  • Nursing
  • Health policy
  • Education
  • Agriculture
  • Food systems
  • Climate
  • Water and sanitation
  • Technology
  • Gender equity
  • Economic policy
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Academia
  • Philanthropy
  • Private-sector organisations
  • Public-sector institutions

The programme calls this broader approach Health++.

Understanding the Health++ Concept

WomenLift Health defines Health++ as the recognition that sustainable improvements in health require coordinated action across interconnected fields that shape and enable health.

These include areas such as:

  • Climate change
  • Food systems
  • Agriculture
  • Water and sanitation
  • Education
  • Economic policy
  • Gender equity
  • Technology

The Health++ approach is based on the understanding that health challenges cannot always be solved within the boundaries of the health sector alone.

For example, health outcomes can be influenced by whether people have access to nutritious food, clean water, safe environments, education, economic opportunities, technology and equitable services.

The Leadership Journey therefore seeks leaders who can think beyond professional silos and work across interconnected systems.

Why Health++ Matters

The programme identifies several important relationships between health and other sectors.

Health and Climate

Climate change can influence disease patterns, nutrition, environmental conditions and people’s ability to access healthcare.

Rising temperatures, extreme weather events and pollution can create additional health risks and increase pressure on health systems.

Women leaders working at the intersection of climate and health can therefore contribute to solutions that address both environmental and health challenges.

Health and Agriculture

Agriculture and food systems have direct implications for nutrition, livelihoods and health.

Food systems can influence problems ranging from malnutrition to obesity while also affecting rural communities and economies.

Cross-sectoral leadership can help address these challenges more effectively.

Health and Gender

Gender influences access to healthcare, health decision-making and leadership.

Understanding power dynamics and gender-related barriers is therefore important for developing health systems that are more equitable.

Women leaders can play a significant role in identifying and addressing these structural challenges.

Health and Technology

Technology is increasingly changing healthcare delivery, diagnostics and access to services.

Digital health tools can create new opportunities while also raising questions about accessibility, equity and inclusion.

Leaders who understand both health systems and technology can help ensure innovation contributes to better and more equitable outcomes.

Developing Women Leaders Across Health++

The programme seeks to develop leaders who can:

  • Collaborate across sectors
  • Think beyond traditional professional boundaries
  • Build coalitions
  • Understand complex systems
  • Identify catalytic leverage points
  • Influence institutions
  • Strengthen their leadership presence
  • Create sustainable health impact

This approach is intended to prepare women leaders to address complex problems that require cooperation between multiple sectors and stakeholders.

Core Elements of the WomenLift Health Leadership Journey

The programme consists of several interconnected components.

1. Health Leadership Project

The Health Leadership Project (HLP) is a central component of the Journey.

Participants enter the programme with an idea for a project that addresses a health-related challenge.

The project gives each participant an opportunity to design and lead an initiative that draws upon their:

  • Expertise
  • Professional network
  • Passion
  • Creativity
  • Leadership capabilities

The goal is to turn leadership learning into practical health impact.

Developing the Health Leadership Project

Participants work on several components of their project, including:

  • A Theory of Change
  • Stakeholder constellation mapping
  • An implementation plan

They receive guidance from:

  • A mentor
  • An HLP reviewer
  • Global health experts within the WomenLift Health team and network

The implementation phase begins during the latter part of the Leadership Journey.

Participants present their project’s development and early outcomes during the Lift-Off event.

The project does not have to be fully completed by the end of the Journey. Participants are expected to continue implementation beyond the programme where appropriate.

Three Principles for the Health Leadership Project

WomenLift Health identifies three major guidelines for HLP projects.

1. Improve Health Outcomes

Projects should focus on improving health outcomes and incorporate gender considerations into interventions, policies and systems.

Participants should consider differences in:

  • Health burdens
  • Risks
  • Access to care
  • Experiences
  • Outcomes

2. Strengthen Leadership

The project should provide an opportunity for participants to apply and strengthen their leadership capabilities.

Participants are encouraged to balance:

  • Personal control
  • Influence
  • Collaboration
  • Resource mobilisation
  • Sustainable impact

3. Address Health Challenges Through a Systems Lens

Participants should channel their passion into addressing a public health challenge while considering:

  • Structures
  • Policies
  • Stakeholders
  • Root causes
  • Systems
  • Long-term sustainability
  • Scalability

This approach is designed to move projects beyond short-term interventions toward sustainable change.

2. Learning Touchpoints

Learning Touchpoints are facilitated virtual and in-person group sessions.

They use interactive and workshop-style approaches rather than relying exclusively on lectures.

Participants explore:

  • Leadership frameworks
  • Leadership research
  • Practical leadership tools
  • Personal development
  • Professional growth
  • Health leadership priorities
  • Relevant sector issues
  • Health Leadership Projects

The sessions also create opportunities for participants to learn from one another.

The cohort’s diversity is therefore an important part of the learning experience.

3. Mentoring Touchpoints

Participants will also receive group mentoring from experienced senior leaders.

WomenLift Health identifies mentors from different:

  • Professional backgrounds
  • Health sectors
  • Disciplines
  • Career trajectories

Mentoring groups consist of several cohort members and a mentor.

Mentors are matched with participants based on complementary backgrounds, professional trajectories and, in some cases, Health Leadership Project topics.

The mentor serves as a technical and career resource throughout the Journey.

4. One-on-One Executive Coaching

Individual coaching is another major feature of the programme.

Each participant is paired with an executive coach who works with her individually.

The coaching relationship helps participants:

  • Identify strengths
  • Understand areas for development
  • Navigate change
  • Respond to new leadership challenges
  • Strengthen leadership effectiveness
  • Prepare for future leadership responsibilities

Leadership-style assessments, including a 360-rater evaluation, are used to inform coaching conversations.

This provides participants with structured feedback about their leadership capabilities and helps them identify areas they may wish to strengthen.

The combination of mentoring and coaching gives participants both:

  • A broader professional support network; and
  • Personalised leadership-development guidance.

5. In-Person Leadership Immersion

The Leadership Immersion is a three-day experiential learning event held several months into the Journey.

The Immersion gives participants the opportunity to move beyond virtual learning and engage directly with their cohort.

Activities include:

  • Dynamic discussions
  • Practical exercises
  • Real-world leadership examples
  • Reflection
  • Peer learning
  • Application of leadership concepts

The 2027 programme schedule identifies the Immersion as taking place from 13–16 April 2027, with travel days on 12 April and 17 April.

The specific location will be communicated to selected cohort members closer to the event, but it will be somewhere in Southern Africa.

6. Leadership Lift-Off

The Leadership Lift-Off takes place toward the end of the Journey.

It is designed to celebrate the cohort’s development and prepare participants for the next stage of their leadership journey.

The programme describes both public and private Lift-Off experiences.

Public Lift-Off

Participants reflect on their leadership development throughout the year and present their Health Leadership Projects to:

  • Fellow cohort members
  • Other health audiences
  • Relevant stakeholders

Private Lift-Off

The private Lift-Off is a two-day event focused on celebrating the cohort’s growth and preparing participants for the next phase of their leadership.

The programme information provided lists the Lift-Off as 14–15 March 2028, with travel days on 13 March and 16 March.

Applicants should carefully review the official programme calendar because the dates provided extend beyond the stated February 2026–March 2027 programme-duration description on the webpage.

Lifelong Leadership Community

Completing the Leadership Journey does not mark the end of participants’ relationship with WomenLift Health.

Those who successfully complete the Journey become Global Fellows and join a lifelong network of women leaders.

The network provides continuing opportunities for:

  • Peer support
  • Professional collaboration
  • Regional networking
  • Global networking
  • Mentorship
  • Leadership exchange
  • Advocacy for women’s leadership

Participants therefore become part of a community that continues beyond the formal programme.

Diversity, Inclusion and Representation

Inclusion is a central value of WomenLift Health.

The organisation states that transformative leadership should:

  • Advocate for women
  • Give women a voice
  • Represent women with diverse lived experiences

WomenLift Health encourages applications from:

  • Minorities
  • Historically marginalised communities
  • Underrepresented communities

within the countries served by the programme.

The organisation also seeks diversity across:

  • Sectors
  • Disciplines
  • Cultures
  • Professional backgrounds
  • Lived experiences

This means the Southern Africa Leadership Journey is not designed around one narrow professional profile.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet all of the stated eligibility requirements.

1. Applicants Must Identify as Women

The programme is specifically designed for women leaders.

Applicants must identify as women to qualify for consideration.

2. English Fluency

Applicants must demonstrate confidence and fluency in both written and verbal English.

This is important because participants are expected to:

  • Express emotions and personal experiences
  • Participate in reflective conversations
  • Engage in complex interpersonal discussions
  • Understand and apply leadership-development concepts
  • Participate actively in group sessions

3. Citizenship, Residence and Employment

Applicants must be citizens who reside and work in one of the following countries:

  • Angola
  • Botswana
  • Lesotho
  • Malawi
  • Mozambique
  • Namibia
  • South Africa
  • eSwatini
  • Zambia
  • Zimbabwe

Applicants outside these countries do not meet the stated country eligibility requirement for the 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey.

4. Time-Zone Requirement

Applicants must live within CAT, plus or minus one hour, for at least 75% of the Leadership Journey.

WomenLift Health considers time-zone compatibility essential because participants need to attend scheduled learning touchpoints and interact with their peers.

5. Professional Experience

Applicants must be mid-career leaders with between 10 and 25 years of work experience in Health++.

This requirement distinguishes the Leadership Journey from programmes aimed at students, recent graduates or early-career professionals.

The programme is intended for experienced professionals who are ready to deepen their leadership influence.

What Does “10–25 Years of Experience in Health++” Mean?

The requirement should not necessarily be interpreted as requiring 10–25 years of work exclusively within hospitals, medical institutions or traditional public health organisations.

WomenLift Health’s Health++ definition is intentionally broad.

Relevant professional experience can involve interconnected sectors such as:

  • Climate
  • Agriculture
  • Food systems
  • Water and sanitation
  • Education
  • Economic policy
  • Gender
  • Technology

The important consideration is the relationship between the applicant’s work and health impact.

Professional Diversity Within the Cohort

WomenLift Health intends to create a diverse cohort representing different sectors, including:

  • Public sector
  • Private sector
  • Academia
  • Non-governmental organisations
  • Philanthropy

This diversity is intended to strengthen cross-sector collaboration and expose participants to perspectives outside their immediate professional environments.

Application Requirements

A complete application must include a letter of recommendation.

The preferred recommender is the applicant’s supervisor.

However, if an applicant cannot obtain a recommendation from her direct supervisor, she may submit a letter from:

  • A senior leader within her current organisation; or
  • A leader in the health community who has experience working with her.

The letter should address the applicant’s:

Leadership Contributions

The recommender should describe significant contributions the applicant has made to her professional field that demonstrate leadership capacity.

Distinguishing Personal Qualities

The recommendation should identify the applicant’s strongest personal quality and explain how that quality distinguishes her as a candidate.

Leadership Development Potential

The recommender should explain how participation in the Leadership Journey could help the applicant strengthen her leadership knowledge and skills.

The recommendation letter must be uploaded as part of the application by the application deadline for the application to be considered complete.

The Health Leadership Project Is Particularly Important

Applicants should pay close attention to the Health Leadership Project component when preparing their applications.

WomenLift Health states that the project and its description carry significant weight in the application review process.

Strong applicants are expected to demonstrate:

  • Original thinking
  • A clear mission
  • Leadership potential
  • Understanding of the health challenge
  • Systems thinking
  • Practical ambition
  • Potential for meaningful health impact

Applicants are therefore encouraged to review the official Health Leadership Project materials before beginning the application.

Using Artificial Intelligence in the Application

WomenLift Health acknowledges that applicants increasingly use artificial intelligence tools when preparing applications.

The organisation does not prohibit thoughtful use of AI, but it emphasises that application responses should remain:

  • Specific
  • Contextualised
  • Rooted in the applicant’s actual work
  • Connected to genuine interests
  • Based on realistic goals
  • Reflective of the applicant’s own thinking

Applicants should avoid submitting generic responses that could have been written for anyone.

The organisation notes that vague responses or applications that appear substantially similar to those of other applicants may receive lower ratings in a highly competitive selection process.

Applicants may therefore use technology as a support tool, but their application should demonstrate their own experience, ideas, leadership journey and goals.

Participation Commitments and Expectations

The Leadership Journey offers extensive support at no cost to participants, including:

  • Mentoring
  • Coaching
  • Assessments
  • Virtual learning
  • In-person experiences

Because the programme receives hundreds of applications and has limited places, selected participants are expected to take their commitment seriously.

Accepting a place means agreeing to participate fully.

The programme’s virtual and in-person sessions are designed as live, small-group learning experiences.

Each participant’s presence contributes to the experience of the entire cohort.

Participants should therefore plan their schedules carefully and make every reasonable effort to attend all required sessions.

If an absence becomes unavoidable, participants are expected to inform WomenLift Health as soon as they know they cannot attend.

Applicants should also review the official Terms of Acceptance covering attendance and data policies.

Programme Schedule

The programme includes several major learning milestones and touchpoints.

Applicants should review the official calendar carefully before applying because participation in the required sessions is mandatory.

The programme information states that participants should ensure they can attend all scheduled touchpoints and in-person residencies.

The in-person components involve travel within Southern Africa.

The published calendar identifies:

Leadership Immersion

13–16 April 2027

Travel days:

  • 12 April 2027
  • 17 April 2027

Leadership Lift-Off

14–15 March 2028

Travel days:

  • 13 March 2028
  • 16 March 2028

The exact locations of the in-person residencies will be communicated to selected cohort members closer to the events and will be in Southern Africa.

Why Apply to the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey?

The programme provides an unusual combination of leadership development, professional networking, coaching, mentoring and practical health impact.

Selected participants can benefit from:

Leadership Development

Participants gain frameworks and tools to strengthen their leadership effectiveness.

Executive Coaching

One-on-one coaching provides personalised support for understanding strengths and areas for growth.

Mentorship

Participants learn from experienced leaders working across different health sectors and disciplines.

Peer Network

The cohort provides a community of women leaders who can exchange knowledge, perspectives and professional experiences.

Health Leadership Project

Participants develop and lead a project addressing a real health challenge.

Regional Exposure

The programme brings together women leaders from across Southern Africa.

Long-Term Community

Successful participants become part of a lifelong WomenLift Health network.

Fully Funded Participation

The programme is free, with programme costs and required travel and lodging covered.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should first confirm that they meet every eligibility requirement.

They should then review the programme’s official resources, particularly:

  • Leadership Journey Framework
  • Health Leadership Project Guidelines
  • Frequently Asked Questions
  • Programme Calendar
  • Terms of Acceptance

Applicants should also identify an appropriate recommender and ensure that the recommendation letter can be submitted before the deadline.

The official WomenLift Health application page should be used to submit the application.

Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM CAT.

APPLY HERE!

Applicants with questions about eligibility can contact:

southernafricajourney@WomenLifthealth.org

Who Qualifies for the 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey?

Category of eligible people

The programme is designed for mid-career women leaders working in health and interconnected Health++ fields.

Eligible applicants must:

  • Identify as women.
  • Have 10–25 years of work experience.
  • Work in Health++ or an interconnected field affecting health.
  • Be citizens of an eligible Southern African country.
  • Reside and work in that eligible country.
  • Demonstrate strong written and spoken English.
  • Live within CAT, plus or minus one hour, for at least 75% of the programme.
  • Be willing and able to participate fully in the programme.
  • Submit the required recommendation letter.

Eligible countries

Applicants must be citizens who reside and work in:

  1. Angola
  2. Botswana
  3. Lesotho
  4. Malawi
  5. Mozambique
  6. Namibia
  7. South Africa
  8. eSwatini
  9. Zambia
  10. Zimbabwe

Race, ethnicity and continental eligibility

The programme does not specify a race or ethnicity restriction in the eligibility criteria provided.

However, WomenLift Health explicitly encourages applications from minorities and historically marginalised and underrepresented communities in the countries it serves.

Geographically, the programme is specifically targeted at Southern Africa, rather than being open to applicants from all African countries or all continents.

Visit HERE to learn more about the WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey.

 

Important Deadline

The application deadline is:

18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM Central Africa Time (CAT).

Applicants should ensure that the complete application, including the required recommendation letter, is submitted before the deadline.

Because the programme is highly competitive and places are limited, applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to complete their application.

APPLY HERE!

Conclusion

The WomenLift Health 2027 Southern Africa Leadership Journey offers a comprehensive leadership-development opportunity for experienced women leaders seeking to increase their influence and create meaningful health impact across Southern Africa.

The programme goes beyond conventional professional training by combining leadership education, mentoring, executive coaching, peer learning, experiential residencies and a practical Health Leadership Project. Participants are given the opportunity to reflect on their leadership journey, develop new skills, build influential relationships and apply their learning to a real-world health challenge.

Its Health++ approach is particularly significant because it recognises that sustainable health improvements require collaboration across sectors such as climate change, agriculture, food systems, education, technology, gender equity, economic policy and water and sanitation.

For eligible women with 10–25 years of professional experience, the programme provides an opportunity to strengthen leadership capabilities while joining a diverse network of women leaders from across Southern Africa.

Participation is free, and programme costs, including required travel and lodging, are covered. However, selected participants must be prepared to make the necessary time commitment and attend the required virtual and in-person sessions.

Women who are citizens, residents and workers in Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, eSwatini, Zambia or Zimbabwe, meet the professional-experience requirement, are confident in English and satisfy the time-zone requirement should consider applying.

The application deadline is 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM CAT. Prospective applicants should carefully review the official programme calendar, eligibility requirements, Health Leadership Project guidelines and application instructions before submitting their applications.

For women leaders ready to deepen their leadership influence, expand their regional network and translate their expertise into sustainable health impact, the WomenLift Health Southern Africa Leadership Journey offers a significant platform for professional and personal transformation.

item.content:encoded:
Jesus College, University of Cambridge is inviting applications for three Research Fellowships for early-career researchers who are nearing completion of their PhD or have recently started their postdoctoral careers.

The fellowships provide an opportunity to spend three years developing research within the academic environment of the University of Cambridge, with a starting remuneration of £32,882, additional benefits and research support.

Two of the fellowships are available across selected Arts and Humanities subjects, while one fellowship is available in the Sciences.

About the Jesus College Research Fellowships

The Research Fellowships are designed for researchers at the early stages of their academic careers.

The fellowships are normally three years in duration and are expected to commence on 1 October 2027.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for candidates who are:

  • Graduate students in the latter stages of research leading to a PhD; or
  • Postdoctoral researchers who have recently been awarded their PhD.

Jesus College notes that candidates who have undertaken more than five years of full-time research are unlikely to be considered. However, the College may consider exceptions where candidates are able to present a case explaining their circumstances as part of the application.

Research Fellowship Areas

Arts Research Fellowships

Two Research Fellowships are available in the following subject areas:

  • Anglo-Saxon, Norse and Celtic (ASNC)
  • Education Studies
  • English
  • Law
  • Modern Languages
  • Theology

Applicants should ensure that their proposed research fits clearly within one of the advertised subject areas.

Science Research Fellowship

A separate Research Fellowship is available in the Sciences.

The Science fellowship provides an opportunity for an early-career researcher to develop their research within the Cambridge academic environment.

Who Should Apply?

The fellowships are intended for brilliant early-career researchers who are beginning to establish themselves as independent scholars.

Applicants may be:

  • Current PhD students who are approaching completion of their doctoral research.
  • Researchers who have recently completed a PhD.
  • Early-career postdoctoral researchers.

Candidates who have undertaken more than five years of full-time research are generally unlikely to be considered, although exceptions may be possible.

The College is looking for researchers who can demonstrate the importance and potential of their current and proposed research.

Fellowship Benefits

Successful candidates will receive several financial and academic benefits throughout the fellowship.

£32,882 Starting Remuneration

The remuneration for a Research Fellow is determined by reference to the University of Cambridge salary scale and starts at £32,882.

Three-Year Fellowship

The fellowship provides funding and support for three years, normally commencing on 1 October 2027.

This gives early-career researchers valuable time to develop their research, publications and academic profile.

Free Meals

Research Fellows receive a free dinner or lunch at Jesus College, regardless of whether they live in College or elsewhere.

Research Benefits

Certain research-related expenses may be reimbursed, providing additional support for fellows undertaking their academic work.

Pension

Research Fellows may also be eligible to join the University Pension Scheme.

Application Requirements

Candidates will need to complete the application process through the Jesus College Research Fellowship application system.

Applications must include the required information and supporting materials.

Shortlisted candidates will subsequently be asked to provide:

  • One sample of written work, up to a maximum of 40,000 words.
  • A 500-word statement explaining the importance of their current and proposed research.
  • Reports from two referees.

Applicants should therefore begin preparing their research materials and contacting potential referees well ahead of the deadline.

What Should Your Research Statement Demonstrate?

The 500-word statement provides shortlisted candidates with an opportunity to explain why their research matters.

Applicants should use this space to clearly communicate:

  • The significance of their current research.
  • The direction of their proposed research.
  • Why the proposed work is important.
  • How their research could contribute to their academic field.
  • Their potential as an early-career researcher.

A clear and focused research proposal can help demonstrate the intellectual value and future potential of the candidate’s work.

Application Timeline

Applications Open: 3 August 2026

Application Deadline: 30 September 2026

Closing Time: 5:00 PM

Fellowship Start Date: 1 October 2027

Duration: Three years

Location: Jesus College, Cambridge, United Kingdom

How to Apply

Applications are submitted online through the Jesus College Research Fellowship application portal.

Application Portal

Apply through the Jesus College Research Fellowship Portal

Applicants can also find additional information about the vacancies and fellowship opportunities on the College’s official website.

Jesus College Vacancies and Fellowships

Important Information for Applicants

Candidates should carefully review the official fellowship details before applying.

In particular, applicants should consider their career stage. These fellowships are specifically intended for early-career researchers, and candidates with more than five years of full-time research are unlikely to be considered unless they can provide a convincing explanation for an exception.

Shortlisted applicants should also be prepared to submit substantial written work of up to 40,000 words and a concise 500-word research statement.

It is therefore advisable to prepare application materials well before the deadline and ensure that referees have sufficient time to submit their reports.

Why Apply?

The Jesus College Research Fellowships provide an opportunity for emerging researchers to develop their academic careers within one of the world’s most recognised university environments.

Beyond the financial remuneration, fellows can benefit from the College’s academic community, research support and opportunities to interact with researchers across different disciplines.

For researchers transitioning from doctoral study into independent research, a three-year fellowship can provide valuable time to strengthen their research portfolio, develop publications and establish themselves within their field.

Conclusion

The Jesus College Cambridge Research Fellowships 2027 offer three early-career researchers the opportunity to undertake supported research at Jesus College, University of Cambridge.

With a starting remuneration of £32,882, a three-year fellowship, research-related benefits, free College meals and potential access to the University Pension Scheme, the opportunity provides substantial support for researchers at the beginning of their academic careers.

The fellowships are open across the Sciences, ASNC, Education Studies, English, Law, Modern Languages and Theology, making the opportunity relevant to researchers from a range of academic disciplines.

If you are completing your PhD or have recently received your doctorate and are looking for an opportunity to develop your research in Cambridge, this fellowship is worth considering.

Application Deadline: 30 September 2026 at 5:00 PM.
